Steam compatibility

Feature: Launcher compatibility system (frankea/Whisky#41) Last updated: 12 January 2026

Note: This document references issue numbers from this fork (frankea/Whisky) and from the original upstream project (whisky-app/whisky). Upstream references are retained for historical context. Report new issues to rolling7ho/Vodka.

Overview

Steam is the most commonly used launcher with Vodka and accounts for the largest share of launcher compatibility reports. This guide describes the recommended configuration and the known failure modes.

Recommended configuration

Step 1: Create a dedicated Steam bottle

  1. Create a new bottle with the name "Steam" and Windows version Windows 10 (recommended), at the default location.
  2. Open Config → Launcher Compatibility and enable Launcher Compatibility Mode.
  3. Set Detection Mode to Automatic. Launching Steam should then report "Detected Launcher: Steam".

Step 2: Install Steam

  1. Download SteamSetup.exe, the Windows installer, from https://store.steampowered.com/about/.
  2. Select Bottle → Run, choose SteamSetup.exe and accept the default installation path (C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\).
  3. Steam starts automatically after installation. If steamwebhelper.exe fails, see the first issue below.

Step 3: Configure graphics and network settings

  1. Leave the graphics backend on Recommended. Steam's own processes (steam.exe, steamwebhelper.exe, steamservice.exe, gameoverlayui64.exe) receive DXVK through per-executable overrides, so the client renders through DXVK while games retain the bottle's backend. When the D3DMetal payload is installed, the recommended backend is D3DMetal, which DirectX 12 games require. A game started from the Vodka library, from vodka launch or from a vodka:// link receives its own settings from the Programs tab and the game database, applied to its own executables regardless of which process starts it. On a runtime without the D3DMetal payload, Play switches the bottle to DXVK. Importing the Game Porting Toolkit later restores the recommended backend once, with a note in the bottle's graphics settings, unless DXVK was selected explicitly. Setting the entire bottle to DXVK disables Direct3D 12 for every game when the payload is deployed; do this only for a bottle whose games all require DXVK.
  2. In Config → Launcher Compatibility, set the network timeout to 90 seconds.
  3. In the same section, enable GPU Spoofing with the NVIDIA vendor, which provides the best compatibility.

Step 4: Verify the configuration

  1. In Config → Launcher Compatibility, select Generate Diagnostics Report.

  2. Confirm the critical settings:

    LC_ALL = en_US.UTF-8                      # required; prevents steamwebhelper failure
STEAM_DISABLE_CEF_SANDBOX = 1             # required; CEF under Wine
STEAM_RUNTIME = 0                         # required; Steam Runtime under Wine
DXVK_ASYNC = 1                            # UI performance

  3. Review the reported warnings. "Configuration is optimal" indicates a complete setup; any warning requires the corresponding change.

Common issues

Issue 1: "steamwebhelper is not responding"

This is the most frequent Steam issue.

Symptoms

  • The Steam window reports an error immediately after launch.
  • A dialog states that steamwebhelper.exe is not responding, and the restart and wait options do not help.
  • The Steam interface is unusable.

Cause

Steam's Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) fails when the locale does not specify UTF-8 encoding, when ICU fails to initialise, or when date and time parsing encounters an unexpected format.

Solution

  1. Open Config → Launcher Compatibility and enable compatibility mode.
  2. Set Locale Override to English.
  3. Generate diagnostics and confirm LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8.

The .UTF-8 suffix is required. en_US alone does not resolve the failure.

LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8   # correct
LC_ALL=en_US         # incorrect; steamwebhelper still fails

If the failure persists, delete the Steam installation, create a new bottle with compatibility mode enabled before installation, install Steam again and verify the locale before the first launch.

Related issues: whisky-app/whisky#946, #1224, #1241.

Issue 2: Downloads stall at 99 percent

Symptoms

  • Progress reaches 99 percent and does not complete.
  • The "Download starting…" message repeats.
  • Steam must be restarted to continue.
  • The behaviour occurs with several games.

Cause

Wine's HTTP implementation misbehaves with persistent connections under some conditions, so downloads time out before completion.

Solution

  1. Open Config → Launcher Compatibility and set Network Timeout to 90 seconds or higher, then restart Steam. The timeout configures WINHTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, and WINHTTP_RECEIVE_TIMEOUT is set to twice that value.
  2. Alternatively, in Steam open Settings → Downloads, select a different download region, pause and resume the download, and clear the download cache.

Longer timeouts prevent premature connection closure. Vodka does not set WINE_FORCE_HTTP11 or WINE_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_SERVER; earlier versions of this guide listed variables that no shipped runtime reads.

Related issues: whisky-app/whisky#1148, #1072, #991, #1222.

Issue 3: Steam disconnects repeatedly

Symptoms

  • "No connection" errors occur every few minutes.
  • Reconnection is required repeatedly, and download progress is lost.
  • The friends list disconnects.

Cause

Network keepalive timeouts and TLS handshake behaviour under Wine.

Solution

  1. Raise the network timeout to 120 seconds or more.
  2. Generate diagnostics and confirm that the locale and sandbox variables listed under Step 4 are present. Vodka does not set WINE_ENABLE_SSL or WINE_SSL_VERSION_MIN.
  3. In System Settings → Network, confirm a stable connection and temporarily disable any VPN for testing.

Related issues: whisky-app/whisky#1176, #954.

Issue 4: Steam interface is blurry or stutters

Symptoms

  • Text appears blurry or pixelated.
  • Interface animations stutter and scrolling is uneven.
  • Window dragging lags.

Solution

  1. Enable DXVK Async in Config → DXVK and restart Steam. DXVK provides better GPU acceleration for the Steam interface.
  2. If text remains blurry, adjust the DPI under Config → Wine → DPI Configuration, selecting 96 DPI (standard) or 192 DPI (Retina).

Related issues: whisky-app/whisky#1256, #1233.

Issue 5: Steam starts without a visible interface

Symptoms

  • The Steam process runs but no window appears, or the window is blank.
  • Notification sounds are audible.

Solution

  1. Select Bottle → Kill All Processes.
  2. Enable compatibility mode if it is not already enabled.
  3. Enable DXVK, disable Metal validation if enabled, and enable Sequoia compatibility mode on macOS 15 or later.
  4. Generate diagnostics and confirm CEF_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1.

If the interface remains invisible, delete Steam, reinstall it, and inspect ~/Library/Logs/com.rolling7ho.Vodka/ for errors.

Related issues: whisky-app/whisky#1183, #1009.

macOS 15.4 and later

Symptoms

  • Steam worked on macOS 15.3 and fails to start after updating to 15.4 or 15.4.1.
  • Wine preloader threads remain blocked.
  • Mach port timeouts occur.

Cause

Apple changed Mach port and threading behaviour in macOS 15.4, which breaks Wine's process creation.

Solution

  1. Enable Config → Metal → Sequoia Compatibility Mode.

  2. Generate diagnostics and confirm the macOS version and the following variables:

    WINEFSYNC = 0
STEAM_RUNTIME = 0
CEF_DISABLE_SANDBOX = 1

  3. Terminate all Wine processes and relaunch Steam.

Related issues: whisky-app/whisky#1372, #1310, #1307.

Advanced configuration

Launch options

For individual games started through Steam, open the game's Properties and set launch options. Common values:

-windowed    force windowed mode
-dx11        force Direct3D 11
-nojoy       disable joystick support
-novid       skip introductory videos

Big Picture mode

Big Picture generally works with compatibility mode enabled. Enable DXVK for performance, connect the controller before launching, and exit through the Steam menu rather than forcing the process to quit.

Steam Workshop

Workshop content generally works with compatibility mode enabled. If it fails, raise the network timeout to 180 seconds, confirm that no firewall blocks the download, and install the content manually as a fallback.

Steam Cloud

Cloud saves are generally functional. Confirm that the game has Cloud enabled under Properties → Updates, and test synchronisation by launching the same game from a second bottle.

Performance tuning

Frame rate

  • Enable DXVK and DXVK Async.
  • Leave the DXVK HUD off unless diagnosing a problem.
  • Enable the shader cache after the first run to reduce stuttering.

Stability

  • Set Enhanced Sync to ESync under Config → Wine.
  • Use Windows 10, which is the most tested Windows version.
  • Enable AVX only for games that require it.

Download throughput

  • Set the network timeout to 120 to 180 seconds.
  • Select a geographically close download region.
  • Clear the Steam download cache.
  • Prefer a wired connection where possible.

Pre-report checklist

Before reporting a Steam issue, confirm the following:

  • Launcher Compatibility Mode is enabled.
  • The locale is en_US.UTF-8.
  • DXVK is enabled.
  • The network timeout is at least 90 seconds.
  • Sequoia Compatibility Mode is enabled on macOS 15 or later.
  • A diagnostics report has been generated and its warnings reviewed.
  • The issue reproduces in a clean bottle.
  • Wine logs have been checked for errors.

Known limitations

Supported: Steam client features (store, library, friends), game downloads, most Direct3D 9, 10 and 11 games, Workshop content, Cloud saves in most cases, achievements and screenshots.

Limited: Steam Input controller configuration, the Steam overlay (game dependent).

Unsupported: broadcasting, Remote Play and VR.

Game compatibility: Direct3D 9 and 11 games generally work well, older titles work well, and Direct3D 12 titles vary. Multiplayer with kernel-level anti-cheat varies by title, and VR titles are unsupported.

Reporting issues

Include the following:

  1. The diagnostics report, attached to the issue.
  2. The Steam version and build date (Help → About Steam).
  3. The exact error message and the point at which it occurs (sign-in, download, launch).
  4. Reproduction steps.
  5. System details: macOS version, Mac model and available disk space.

Example report:

**Issue:** Steam downloads stall at 99 percent

**System:**
- macOS 15.4.1
- M2 Pro MacBook Pro
- Vodka version 4.x
- Steam version: December 2025 build

**Configuration:**
- Launcher Compatibility: enabled
- Network Timeout: 60 seconds
- DXVK: enabled

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Queue a large game download.
2. Progress reaches 99 percent.
3. The download stalls indefinitely.
4. Restarting Steam resumes the download, which stalls again at 99 percent.

**Diagnostics report:** attached

**Attempted fixes:**
- Changed the download region; no change.
- Raised the timeout to 90 seconds; the download still stalls.
- Cleared the download cache; no change.

Vodka is free and open source, requires no reboot, integrates with macOS, and applies the compatibility configuration described above automatically once launcher compatibility is enabled.

FAQ

Can an existing Steam library be reused? Games must be downloaded again, or restored from a Steam backup. Save files may not transfer automatically, and individual games may require configuration.

Does Steam report that the machine runs macOS? No. Steam reports the Windows version presented by Wine.

Does the Workshop work? Generally yes. Raise the network timeout for large Workshop items.

Does the Steam overlay work? This depends on the game; some titles do not render it correctly.

Is game streaming supported? Streaming from this Steam installation to other devices is limited. Streaming to this installation is not recommended, because it adds a second translation layer.

Do achievements work? Yes.

Is the Steam Controller supported? Partially. Basic controller input works; advanced Steam Input features may not.

Does anti-cheat work? This depends on the game. VAC is reported to work generally, while EAC and BattlEye are frequently blocked. Consult ProtonDB for a specific title.

Monitoring and maintenance

Weekly: Steam updates automatically. Check for Vodka updates and review new configuration warnings.

After a macOS update: confirm that Steam launches, that steamwebhelper.exe starts, that downloads complete, and regenerate diagnostics if problems appear.

After a Wine update: test compatibility, recreate the bottle if failures are severe, and review the issue tracker for known problems with the runtime version.

Healthy indicators: Steam launches within 10 seconds, store pages load promptly, downloads sustain their throughput, and games launch without delay.

Warning signs: launches taking longer than 30 seconds, frequent disconnects, downloads that consistently stall, and high CPU usage while idle.

Recovery

Reset Steam within the bottle

  1. Select Bottle → Open in Finder.
  2. Navigate to drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Steam/.
  3. Delete steam.exe and steamwebhelper.exe.
  4. Run SteamSetup.exe again.

Create a fresh bottle

  1. Create a new bottle with compatibility mode enabled before installation.
  2. Install Steam.
  3. Sign in and verify the client before downloading games.

Restore from backup

If Metadata.plist was backed up, replace the current file with the backup, restart Vodka and test Steam.

Save file location

~/Library/Application Support/<Bottle>/drive_c/users/<username>/My Documents/

Most games store saves in the Documents directory. Back it up before recreating a bottle.
